item.title: How One Entomologist's Career Path Was Inspired by a TV Show
item.description: Meet Yuexun Tian, Ph.D., entomologist at Central Life Sciences, expert in arthropod vectors, and our next "Standout Early Career Professional" profile.

item.title: Meet Buzzdetect: An Open-Source AI Tool for Listening to Pollinators
item.description: Buzzdetect uses microphones and machine learning to continuously detect pollinator activity. A new study shows how it can offer a low‑cost way to "listen" for bees in real time.

item.title: What Does It Take to Detect Long-Term Insect Abundance Trends?
item.description: A new study looks at a 29-year moth-trapping effort and suggests a minimum of 15 years of data for detecting true long-term trends in insect populations.

item.title: Endophytic 'Bodyguards': How Insect-Killing Fungi Inside Plants Can Help Manage Pests
item.description: Beneficial fungi living inside plants can act as built‑in bodyguards to weaken pests and boost plant defenses, offering a promising option for integrated pest management programs.

item.title: New Study Busts Myths About Feared Recluse Spiders
item.description: A new study shows brown recluse spiders and relatives are in fact scarce, reluctant to bite, and mostly unlikely to cause the severe harm often attributed to them.

item.title: Vector Guard: An App for Real-Time, Local Guidance on Arthropod-Borne Disease Risk
item.description: A mobile app for local risk info about disease-carrying arthropods took 1st Place in the 2025 ESA Antlion Pit, an innovation competition for entomology-related products and services. Meet the creator of Vector Guard and learn what's next for the app's development.

item.title: Tiny Insect, Big Questions: Is the World's Smallest Dragonfly Splitting Into Two Species?
item.description: A new study of Nannophya pygmaea, a dragonfly with a wingspan about the size of a penny, combines genetics and climate models to explore isolation, habitat shifts, and the gray area between populations and species.

item.title: Lemon Eucalyptus Oil Effective as Tick-Repellent Fabric Spray, Study Shows
item.description: A new study shows that a spray repellent made from lemon eucalyptus oil strongly repels ticks when applied to common fabrics, performing as well as DEET and remaining effective for several days.

item.title: New Research Links Honey Bee Swarms to the Spread of an Invasive Mite
item.description: Tropilaelaps mites can hitch rides on swarming honey bees and reproduce in new colonies, a key discovery in the effort to prevent the parasite's spread beyond Asia.

item.title: New Model Guides Better Mosquito-Trap Placement to Detect West Nile Virus
item.description: Researchers have developed a model to pinpoint the best locations for traps to detect West Nile virus earlier and more accurately.
